hero.headline: Woman charged with attempted murder, arson after Port St. Lucie house fire
hero.body:
A 26-year-old woman faces attempted murder and arson charges following a house fire in Port St. Lucie. Michelle Picard was arrested after the victim discovered smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door.

The investigation revealed that when the victim opened her bedroom door, she found Picard standing nearby. Port St. Lucie police responded to the incident and took Picard into custody. The victim escaped the fire and authorities were able to control the blaze.

Picard is the daughter of the victim, according to investigators. She now faces multiple felony charges including attempted murder and arson. The specific address of the house fire has not been released by authorities.

Port St. Lucie police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the fire. Picard remains in custody as the case moves forward through the criminal justice system. The victim was not reported injured in the incident.

hero.headline: Property Value Growth Declines for Fourth Consecutive Year in Florida County
hero.body:
Property value growth has declined for four consecutive years in a Florida county, according to a new report. The decline marks a significant shift in the real estate market that affects property tax revenues and local government budgets.

The continued decline in property value growth represents a four-year trend that impacts homeowners, local governments, and the broader economy. Property values determine tax assessments that fund schools, public safety, infrastructure, and other essential services. A slowdown in growth means less revenue available for these programs without adjusting millage rates.

The decline comes despite Florida's overall strong real estate market in recent years. The specific county experiencing this trend faces unique challenges that have kept property value increases below historical averages. Property owners in the affected area have seen their home values appreciate at slower rates compared to neighboring counties and the state average.

Local officials will need to address the implications of this trend as they prepare future budgets and make decisions about service levels and tax rates. The four-year decline suggests structural issues rather than temporary market fluctuations. Property appraisers will continue to assess values annually, and county commissioners will set millage rates based on those assessments and budget needs. Residents should expect continued discussions about balancing tax rates with service demands as the county navigates this extended period of slower property value growth.

County officials are evaluating the potential economic and logistical benefits of establishing rocket recovery operations at the Fort Pierce port. cards.headline: Port St. Lucie daughter charged with attempted murder, arson after setting bedroom fire
cards.teaser: A Port St.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder and arson charges after investigators say she set a fire in her mother's home. Michelle Picard, 26, was arrested following an incident in which her mother discovered smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door.

The victim opened her bedroom door and found Picard standing nearby, according to the investigation. Authorities determined that Picard had deliberately set the fire, leading to the serious felony charges. The Port St. Lucie Police Department conducted the investigation that resulted in the arrest.

Picard now faces charges of attempted murder and arson, both serious felonies under Florida law. The attempted murder charge indicates investigators believe the fire was set with intent to kill the victim. Arson charges in Florida carry significant prison sentences, particularly when combined with attempted murder allegations.

The case remains under investigation by Port St. Lucie police. Picard is being held as she awaits court proceedings on the charges. The victim's condition and the extent of damage to the home were not immediately disclosed by authorities.

hero.headline: Body of Vero Beach Library Shooting Suspect Found After Ocean Escape
hero.body:
Authorities recovered the body of a suspect who killed two people at a Vero Beach library before escaping into the ocean. The suspect killed his wife and another man at the library before fleeing to the water.

The incident occurred at a Vero Beach library in Indian River County. After the double homicide, the suspect escaped into the ocean. Search efforts focused on the coastal waters near the crime scene.

The bodies of both victims, including the suspect's wife and an unidentified male, were found at the library. Law enforcement officials launched an immediate search for the suspect after witnesses reported seeing him enter the ocean following the shooting.

The suspect's body was later located by authorities conducting the search operation. The recovery brings an end to the search for the armed suspect who terrorized the Vero Beach community. No further details about the victims' identities or the motive for the killings have been released by investigators.
